definition: A naturalistic environment is a person’s usual real-world setting, where daily activities and stressors occur outside a controlled laboratory or clinic. In mental health research, it refers to studying experiences and responses as they happen in everyday life.

reasons: The packet does not provide an explicit definition of “naturalistic environment”; it only uses the phrase in describing a study context (remote assessment in everyday life).
Claims like “a person’s usual real-world setting” and “outside a controlled laboratory or clinic” are not stated in the packet.

The packet does not support the general statement that, “In mental health research,” the term specifically refers to studying “experiences and responses as they happen in everyday life.” It instead describes using wearable technology to quantify physiological response to psychosocial stress during exams in everyday settings.
The phrase “person’s usual real-world setting” is broader than the packet, which only supports stressors encountered “in the naturalistic environment” or “in everyday life.”
“Outside a controlled laboratory or clinic” is not stated in the packet and adds an unsupported contrast to laboratory/clinic settings.

The definition shifts from defining the environment to describing a research approach (“studying experiences and responses”), which is only indirectly supported by the packet’s example of wearable/EMA assessment in everyday life.
